variants.headline: {{aggressor}} marches on {{ally}}
body: {{aggressor}} has declared war on {{ally}}, a small power allied to this nation. The news reached the ally's market by noon, and the shutters went up before any soldiers came into view. Our soldiers are not in the fighting, and our promise to the ally now stands alone.

variants.headline: One of our small allies is at war
body: One of our small allies is now at war, though the dispatches do not name every banner in the fighting. A carter who drives that road has turned back twice rather than guess who holds the next bridge.

variants.headline: Why the attack on {{ally}} matters
body: The war on {{ally}} is less about the ally than about what {{aggressor}} intends next. A power that declares war on a small state is practicing for a larger one. Every promise we make to a small state is a promise our treasury and our recruits must keep, and the reckoning is already overdue.

variants.headline: {{aggressor}} opens war on {{ally}}
body: Notice to carriers and merchants: war has come to {{ally}}, one of the small powers allied to this nation. Carts headed for its market should turn aside until the fighting stops. {{aggressor}} opened the war, and this nation remains outside it.

variants.headline: An ally is at war. What is our answer?
body: Mark it, {{terms.civic.people}}: {{ally}} is at war, and its people are looking down the road for the help we promised. Our {{terms.civic.government}} should name the wagons, the men and the day they leave, because a promise that arrives after the roads close is no promise at all.

variants.headline: {{cityState}} falls to {{captor}}
body: {{captor}} has taken {{cityState}} by force, and the small power that stood with us now flies a foreign flag. One merchant who sold there has hauled his stock back over the border, and he says the square was full of strangers on his last morning.

variants.headline: An allied city-state is taken
body: Word has come that a foreign army has taken one of our small allies. The dispatches leave names out, but the empty place at the treaty table does not.

variants.headline: What we lost with {{cityState}}
body: {{captor}}'s flag now flies over {{cityState}}, and the road that made the town useful runs through a stranger's country. The drivers who once broke their journeys there now water their horses on this side of the border. If the trade stays away, the innkeepers of {{cityState}} will feel the conquest in their purses long after the soldiers leave.

variants.headline: {{cityState}}, faithful to the last
body: {{cityState}} governed itself among the small powers and chose this nation for its friend, and it never broke that choice, not even at the last. Let the record show the city as it stood in its last season: a free council, a faithful ally, and a gate that opened to no foreign banner until it could hold no longer.

variants.headline: Tell our allies when help can reach them
body: {{captor}} has taken {{cityState}}, and the ally we promised to protect is gone. Our {{terms.civic.government}} should put a number on its promises: how many soldiers, how many days, and what a small town can expect when it calls. Without that number, every future ally is buying hope.

variants.when: cityState !== null && captor !== null && distance !== null
variants.headline: Our ally falls {{distance}} from home
body: {{captor}} has taken {{cityState}}, {{distance}} from our nearest town. A carter in our town has cousins behind those walls, and he has been stopping every traveler on the road home for word of them.

variants.headline: {{cityState}} defects to {{rival}}
body: {{cityState}}, a small power near our borders, has thrown over its alliance with us for one with {{rival}}. Our envoy at that court is folding his letters and pricing a seat on the next cart home.

variants.headline: A neighbor's friendship changes hands
body: A rival has taken over the friendship of a small power on our borders, and our own envoys are already packing. The gate they leave behind now flies another power's colors beside its own.

variants.headline: Would more gold have kept {{cityState}}?
body: {{cityState}} has moved its alliance from us to {{rival}}, and the capital will want to call it an auction lost. The city may have been looking for help with a quarrel of its own, and a larger purse from us would not have settled that. The fault may lie less in our gold than in what our envoys stopped noticing.

variants.headline: The flags came down at {{cityState}}
body: The banner that flew beside {{cityState}}'s own had been ours for as long as the caravans could remember. On the morning the watch changed, a boy on the wall lowered our banner and raised {{rival}}'s without a word. The gate itself never moved; only the road it opened onto did.

variants.headline: A letter from the frontier
body: Madam Editor: my stall sits at the corner where the road runs into {{cityState}}'s market, and from it I count the envoys as they pass. For a season now the visitors in {{rival}}'s cloaks have outnumbered ours, so when the alliance changed this week, the only surprise on my road was that anyone was surprised.

variants.headline: {{cityState}} names us its ally
body: {{cityState}} now calls this nation its ally. Its envoy lost no time asking what we mean to send and when it will arrive.

variants.headline: A small power chooses us
body: A city-state has chosen this nation for its ally. The bond is ours now, and keeping it will take more than the ceremony that made it.

variants.headline: What {{cityState}} opens to us
body: {{cityState}} is our new ally, {{distance}} from the nearest of our towns. Our merchants are already sorting their wares for a first venture into that market. Our envoys should be there while the ceremony is still fresh, before another power's envoy arrives with a heavier purse.

variants.headline: Notice: our envoys succeed in {{cityState}}
body: Notice is given that {{cityState}} has quit the alliance of {{replaced}} and chosen this nation instead. Credit belongs to the {{terms.civic.government}}'s envoys, whose patience and coin did the work. Traders headed for that market may collect a letter of introduction at the foreign office.

variants.headline: Hear it! {{cityState}} stands with us
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}, wherever this news finds you! The city of {{cityState}} has bound itself to this nation! Its council has chosen our friendship! {{cityState}} stands with us, and the news should reach every gate before nightfall!

variants.headline: {{cityState}} walks away from our alliance
body: {{cityState}} has left our alliance, and none has been named to fill the place it held. In the capital, the clerk who keeps the book of friendships has drawn a line through the city's name.

variants.headline: Our ally leaves, and no one follows
body: A small power has ended its alliance with this nation, and no other has been invited into the gap. The chair it kept at our table is vacant now, and vacant chairs invite other guests.

variants.headline: Who lost {{cityState}}?
body: An alliance with {{cityState}} has ended, and the city did not leave us for anyone else. That is the detail the capital should study: a rival did not outbid us, so something in our own conduct wore the friendship thin. Allies are lost by neglect long before they are lost by auction.

variants.headline: The alliance with {{cityState}} ends
body: In this season {{cityState}} set aside its alliance with this nation, and no other power took our place. The city-state still stands among the powers of the world, and its friendship belongs to no one.

variants.headline: The {{cityState}} account, closed
body: Bond with this nation: dissolved.
Successor named: none.
Balance: a free small power, gone from our column, owing us nothing.

variants.headline: {{cityState}} switches its alliance to {{friend}}
body: {{cityState}} has chosen {{friend}} for its ally, and our own alliance there is finished. Our envoy in the square passes his letters to {{friend}}'s man, who takes them with a bow. The bond leaves our hands, but it lands with a declared friend.

variants.headline: An ally passes to a friend
body: A small power close to our border has moved its alliance from us to a nation we call friend. The loss is real, though it is the softest loss an alliance can suffer.

variants.headline: A go-between for {{cityState}}
body: {{cityState}} now looks to {{friend}} instead of us, and the change may yet serve everyone. If a quarrel over a road or a field arises, both towns still have a common friend to carry messages between them. {{friend}} can test the ground before the dispute hardens into a quarrel that nobody can settle.

variants.headline: Notice of a new ally in {{cityState}}
body: For the record: {{cityState}}, {{distance}} from our nearest city, now counts {{friend}} its ally. Our own alliance there closes with the season, and it closes without a quarrel.

variants.headline: {{cityState}} changes allies tonight
body: Among the small powers tonight, {{cityState}} has switched its alliance to {{friend}}. It lies {{distance}} from our nearest border. It was our ally until today. We count the new ally a friend.

variants.headline: {{cityState}} counts us a friend
body: {{cityState}} now counts this nation a friend, though not yet an ally. Its market now admits our traders on the same terms as any friend's, and its council keeps our letters near the top of the pile.

variants.headline: {{cityState}} is friendly no longer
body: Friendship with {{cityState}} has lapsed, and the city no longer counts us among its friends. The welcome at its gate has cooled, and its council has less time for our envoy than it did last season.

variants.headline: Friendship recorded with {{cityState}}
body: Let the record show that friendship between this nation and {{cityState}} begins with this season. The city's scribes have entered the bond in their book, and a copy now rests in our own archive.

variants.headline: We let a friendship lapse
body: Our friendship with {{cityState}} is finished. Goodwill between peoples is kept by showing up, and our envoys stopped showing up seasons ago. The capital deserves an explanation for that, and so does the city.

variants.headline: A word at the fire
body: They say by the fire: let the hearth go cold, and the guest finds another door. So it stands with {{cityState}}.

variants.headline: A deadline comes off {{cityState}}'s board
body: {{cityState}} has taken one of its errands off the board before the deadline. A traveler who had set aside coin for the journey says she will wait a week before spending it on anything else.

variants.headline: A small power's notice board loses a deadline
body: A dated errand has vanished from a small power's board, and the mason who had quoted stone for the work is left with a price on his books for a job that may never be ordered.

variants.headline: Notice: an errand ends in {{cityState}}
body: Merchants and travelers should know that {{cityState}} has dropped one of its posted errands before the deadline. Workmen who quoted a price for it should stop at the gate before laying out more coin on travel.

variants.headline: The missing date on {{cityState}}'s board
body: The errand that {{cityState}} had posted to close on day {{previousDeadline}} is gone from its board. One workman, who had kept his best boots aside for the journey, now says he will not lace them until someone confirms the job exists.

variants.headline: The {{cityState}} deadline is {{turnsLeft}} out
body: An errand on {{cityState}}'s board comes due in {{turnsLeft}}. A hauler has loaded the last of the goods and means to be inside the gate before the board is cleared.

variants.headline: A {{cityState}} errand ends today
body: Today is the last day for the errand {{cityState}} posted. When the sun goes down, the work will be finished or it will be too late.

variants.headline: A small power's errand is nearly due
body: An errand posted by one of the small powers is nearly due. A traveler who hopes to answer it has asked the next cart out of town for a ride as far as the driver will take him.

variants.headline: The {{cityState}} clock hits zero
body: Today is the last day for the {{cityState}} errand. Finish it or don't. The board won't wait.

variants.headline: Hear it! {{turnsLeft}} on the {{cityState}} errand
body: Hear it, everyone with goods or hands in the {{cityState}} errand! {{turnsLeft}} left, and the sand is running! {{turnsLeft}}! Move now, or explain to the gate why you did not!

variants.headline: {{cityState}} posts an errand with a deadline
body: {{cityState}} has posted a fresh errand and given it {{turnsLeft}}. A tanner read the notice twice and then went looking for his partner, since the job would take two pairs of hands.

variants.headline: A new errand, and a deadline
body: A small power's new errand allows {{turnsLeft}}. The clock is already running on it.

variants.headline: New errand posted in {{cityState}}
body: Word from {{cityState}} tonight: a new errand is on its board. It must be done in {{turnsLeft}}. The count has already started.

variants.headline: A clock worth beating
body: {{cityState}} wants its new errand done within {{turnsLeft}}, which leaves room for serious work. A prize with a clock beside it is still a prize, and it will go to whoever starts first. This realm should be the one starting.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} wins the alliance of {{cityState}}
body: {{cityState}} now follows {{civilization}} as its ally. {{civilization}}'s colors went up beside the city's own, {{distance}} from the nearest of our towns.

variants.headline: A great power gains a small friend
body: A great nation has gained an ally among the small powers on our border. That friendship now sits {{distance}} from our nearest town.

variants.headline: A foothold {{distance}} from our walls
body: {{civilization}} has won itself a friend in {{cityState}}, a city {{distance}} from our nearest. Gold and patience did the work, and the same coin will be needed to hold it. That alliance could have been ours, and no power pays that price for a neighbor it does not mean to use.

variants.headline: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}: {{civilization}} wins a neighbor
body: Mark it, {{terms.civic.people}}: nearby {{cityState}} has gone over to {{civilization}}. Carters at this end are asking whose men will meet them on the wool road. Our {{terms.civic.government}} should settle that question before the drivers settle it for themselves.

variants.when: cityState !== null && civilization !== null && replaced !== null
variants.headline: The seat is still warm
body: {{cityState}} has a new ally in {{civilization}}, and every courtesy {{replaced}} once enjoyed there now comes to a different address.

variants.headline: {{aggressor}} makes war on our friend {{cityState}}
body: {{aggressor}} is at war with {{cityState}}, a small power that counts this nation its friend. Its traders have hauled their goods off the road, and none of our soldiers have been called to it.

variants.headline: A friendly city-state under attack
body: War has come to one of the small powers that count this nation a friend. A wool trader camped outside its market now questions every driver about the road ahead, and none of them can promise it is clear.

variants.headline: What the war on {{cityState}} reveals
body: What {{aggressor}} has done to {{cityState}} tells us more about {{aggressor}} than about the city. A power that makes war on a friendly small state has shown how much friendship weighs in its plans. Our own soldiers are not in this war, and they should be studying what just happened next door.

variants.headline: It is told that war came to {{cityState}}
body: They say it at every fire, and the story does not change: {{aggressor}} has gone to war with {{cityState}}, the small state that calls us friend. Our sons are not in that fighting, and the town counts its blessings by the full seats at supper.

variants.headline: War reaches {{cityState}}
body: Notice to traders: war has come to {{cityState}}, a small power that counts this nation a friend. Drivers heading for that market should find a different route. {{aggressor}} began it, and our {{terms.civic.government}} has offered no arms.

variants.headline: Our friend {{cityState}} falls to {{captor}}
body: {{cityState}} has fallen to {{captor}}, taken by conquest. The city counted this nation a friend, and its market, which traded freely with our towns, is now a stranger's outpost.

variants.headline: A friendly city-state is taken
body: A small power that counted this nation a friend has been taken by a foreign army. The dispatches leave some names blank, but the hole in our circle of friends needs no name.

variants.headline: The passing of {{cityState}}
body: The record of the small powers will show {{cityState}} as a friend that did not waver. It held to this nation until the swords reached its streets. Its altars are in other hands now, and the faithful can only pray that the fires are left burning.

variants.headline: Conquest near our borders
body: Tonight, a friendly city-state is in {{captor}}'s hands. The city is under a new flag. Word of the fighting puts it {{distance}} from our nearest city. That is close, and this border should be watched.

variants.headline: Letters from the frontier: {{cityState}} is taken
body: Word from the frontier: {{captor}} has conquered {{cityState}}, a small power in friendship with this nation. Another name leaves the roll of independent powers, and this paper has only sympathy to print.
